_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-25 · Sam checked Sierra in a browser and confirmed she is right again: "Sierra looks great this morning." That closes the problem he reported the night before, where she said Moreno Valley College had no students when it actually has nearly 2,900 — the most of Riverside's three colleges. She had been reading a copy of the numbers taken in June that nobody has updated since, while the real figures refresh every night. Rather than refresh the old copy we deleted it, because two copies of the same fact always drift apart again and a stale number looks exactly like a fresh one. That fix went live together with the two Memory tab features that had been waiting on the same deploy. We had already checked character-by-character that the right code was running and that the automated tests passed — but none of that can tell you whether an answer reads correctly to a person. Only someone looking can, and now someone has.
_status: Deployed, and the Sierra half is confirmed. The Sierra fix and both Memory tab features (Autogenerate reading your whole note, and the Briefing that reads the entries back to you) went live together on 25 August, and Sam checked Sierra in a browser the next morning. The Briefing itself has still never been looked at by a person — it shipped in the same deploy but it is a different screen, so "Sierra looks great" does not cover it. That is on the list below.

items.text: Decide whether SkyView's re-mint queue gets built now. Our recommendation is not yet: nobody has dragged a course yet, so the queue would open empty. A drag or two first would give it something real.
Optional: try a drag in SkyView. It would be the first one ever — no course has been re-homed yet, and the first one tells us whether the detection behind it actually fires.

Press the Briefing button at the top of the Memory tab's Report view. It should write plain-language prose with small numbered links back to the entries it used. Nobody has seen it yet — it went live with the Sierra fix, but it is a different screen.
Two other answers still need your eyes rather than ours: the district roster question for Los Angeles, and a phone check of the Fact Sheet and veteran map.
Next time cpl-chat changes, run the new A/B workflow first. It deploys a candidate to a private copy and compares both against real questions before anything reaches the live site.
34 tests still check that a value is a function's LAST argument rather than that it arrives at all. Four were fixed; the rest go red for the wrong reason when anyone adds a parameter.
The project's own memory file is two and a half times the size it should be, and every session pays for that on startup. It needs prose moved out, not more added.
SkyView's course descriptions still have to be served from a local folder. Sam expects them in the shared database; table-versus-file and who can read them are still open.
A leftover scheduled job from an older session is still queued to merge a pull request that merged long ago. Harmless, but worth clearing.
